The long version contains full proofs of all s
arxiv-1811-09411.creator: Laurent Bulteau, Niels Grüttemeier, Christian Komusiewicz, Manuel Sorge
arxiv-1811-09411.description: Abstract Given an undirected graph G = ( V , E ) G=(V,E) the NP-hard Strong Triadic Closure (STC) problem asks for a labeling of the edges as weak and strong such that at most k k edges are weak and for each induced P 3 P_{3} in G G at least one edge is weak.

arxiv-2205-00005.title: Optically detected magnetic resonance with an open source platform
arxiv-2205-00005.creator: Hossein Babashah, Hoda Shirzad, Elena Losero, Valentin Goblot, Christophe Galland, Mayeul Chipaux
arxiv-2205-00005.description: Abstract Localized electronic spins in solid-state environments form versatile and robust platforms for quantum sensing, metrology and quantum information processing. With optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR), it is possible to prepare and readout highly coherent spin systems, up to room temperature, with orders of magnitude enhanced sensitivities and spatial resolutions compared to induction-based techniques, allowing for single spin manipulations.

arxiv-2209-08328.title: Towards a Better Understanding of OPD Limitations for Higher Sensitivity and Contrast at the VLTI.
arxiv-2209-08328.creator: B. Courtney-Barrer, J. Woillez, R. Laugier, A. Bigioli, N. Schuhler, P. Guajardo, V. Lizana, N. Behara, F. Eisenhauer, M. Ireland, X. Haubois, D. Defrère
arxiv-2209-08328.description: Abstract Precise control of the optical path differences (OPD) in the Very Large Telescope Interferometer (VLTI) was critical for the characterization of the black hole at the center of our Galaxy - leading to the 2020 Nobel prize in physics.

arxiv-2310-14775.title: Many-body quantum interference route to the two-channel Kondo effect: Inverse design for molecular junctions and quantum dot devices
arxiv-2310-14775.creator: Sudeshna Sen, Andrew K. Mitchell
arxiv-2310-14775.description: Abstract Molecular junctions – whether actual single molecules in nanowire break junctions or artificial molecules realized in coupled quantum dot devices – offer unique functionality due to their orbital complexity, strong electron interactions, gate control, and many-body effects from hybridization with the external electronic circuit. Inverse design involves finding candidate structures that perform a desired function optimally.

arxiv-2406-03298.title: L-PR: Exploiting LiDAR Fiducial Marker for Unordered Low Overlap Multiview Point Cloud Registration
arxiv-2406-03298.creator: Yibo Liu, Jinjun Shan, Amaldev Haridevan, Shuo Zhang
arxiv-2406-03298.description: Abstract Point cloud registration is a prerequisite for many applications in computer vision and robotics. Most existing methods focus on the registration of point clouds with high overlap. While some learning-based methods address low overlap cases, they struggle in out-of-distribution scenarios with extremely low overlap ratios.

arxiv-2502-14066.title: Experiment Design with Gaussian Process Regression with Applications to Chance-Constrained Control
arxiv-2502-14066.creator: Sean Anderson, Katie Byl, João P. Hespanha
arxiv-2502-14066.description: Abstract Learning for control in repeated tasks allows for well-designed experiments to gather the most useful data. We consider the setting in which we use a data-driven controller that does not have access to the true system dynamics. Rather, the controller uses inferred dynamics based on the available information.

pmc-11490738.creator: Mary E Bernardin, Jyoti Arora, Paul Schuler, Benjamin Fisher, Joseph Finney, Elizabeth Kendrick, Danielle Lee
pmc-11490738.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). pmc-11608885.title: Biases in Routine Influenza Surveillance Indicators Used to Monitor Infection Incidence and Recommendations for Improvement
pmc-11608885.creator: Oliver Eales, James M McCaw, Freya M Shearer
pmc-11608885.description: BackgroundMonitoring how the incidence of influenza infections changes over time is important for quantifying the transmission dynamics and clinical severity of influenza. Infection incidence is difficult to measure directly, and hence, other quantities which are more amenable to surveillance are used to monitor trends in infection levels, with the implicit assumption that they correlate with infection incidence.

pmc-11611708.title: Identification and Validation of circDOCK1/miR-138-5p/GRB7 Axis for Promoting Breast Cancer Progression
pmc-11611708.creator: Yan Zhang, Mei Yang, Yiping Wang, Junhao Zhao, Pei Yao Lee, Yuhua Ma, Shaohua Qu
pmc-11611708.description: BackgroundNon-coding RNAs have received increasing attention in human tumors, with RNA interaction networks playing important roles in breast cancer. This study aims to explore novel circular RNAs and their mechanisms of biological function in breast cancer.MethodsSix HER2-positive breast cancer tissues and paired normal tissues were obtained for the whole transcriptome RNA sequencing.

pmc-12365259.title: Evaluation of sports teaching quality in universities based on fuzzy decision support system
pmc-12365259.creator: Kunjian Han, Jian Wan
pmc-12365259.description: Sports teaching in universities relies on staff experience, training modes., evaluated by the student’s performance and competitive outcomes. The teaching quality assessment requires a large volume of data related to teaching patterns, training. A Teaching Convoluted Quality Assessment Model (TCQAM) is proposed in this article to provide a robust teaching quality assessment.

pmc-12419217.title: Gaps in Low-Dose Aspirin Use for Preeclampsia Prevention: Insights and Clinical Implications
pmc-12419217.creator: Nadir Ganem, Maya Frank Wolf, Raneen Sawaid Kayal, Ala Aiob, Dina Gumin, Lior Lowenstein, Inshirah Sgayer
pmc-12419217.description: ObjectiveTo evaluate real-world prescribing patterns of low-dose aspirin for preeclampsia prevention among pregnant women who met the Israeli or American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) guideline criteria for preeclampsia prophylaxis, and to identify disparities and missed opportunities in implementing risk-based prophylaxis in a diverse obstetric population.

pmc-12420925.title: The Role of The Xihuang Pill in Inhibiting Triple-Negative Breast Cancer Through Immunogenic Cell Death
pmc-12420925.creator: Xingchao Xu, XiangQi Li
pmc-12420925.description: Modern Western medicine uses surgeries, chemotherapy, targeted therapy, and radiotherapy to inhibit breast cancer cells through pathways such as apoptosis, necrosis, and autophagy. However, for triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), a highly aggressive subtype lacking targeted therapies, conventional chemotherapy often leads to severe side effects and drug resistance, thereby limiting its clinical efficacy.

pmc-12423883.title: A Structure-Based Approach for Predicting Odor Similarity of Molecules via Docking Simulations with Human Olfactory Receptors
pmc-12423883.creator: Hirotada Kaneshiro, Masakazu Sato, Airi Tanaka, Shuya Nakata, Yoshiko Aihara, Hirotaka Kitoh-Nishioka, Yoshiharu Mori, Shigenori Tanaka
pmc-12423883.description: The mechanisms underlying human odor recognition remain largely unclear, making it challenging to predict the scent of a novel molecule based solely on its molecular structure. Unlike taste, which is classified into a limited number of categories, odor perception is highly complex and lacks universally defined labels, rendering absolute odor classification inherently ambiguous.

pmc-13178337.title: Reducing respiratory motion artifacts in gadoxetate disodium-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (EOB-MRI): assessing assisted breath-holding effectiveness
pmc-13178337.creator: Xiao-Yue Zhang, Chuan Liu, Xing-Yu Wang, Hong-Sheng Liu, Dan Liu, Dan-Feng Xiang, Yun Mao, Rui Jin, Ren-Qiang Yu
pmc-13178337.description: BackgroundGadoxetate disodium-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (EOB-MRI) is a critical modality in hepatobiliary diagnostics, providing high-resolution imaging of hepatic lesions and functional assessment of the liver. Despite its clinical benefits, respiratory motion artifacts in the hepatic arterial phase of EOB-MRI remain a major clinical challenge, reducing diagnostic accuracy.

pmc-13431544.title: Repair of Tibial Fractures in Field Settings Using Full Limb Cast with Double Transfixation Pinning in 11 Beef Cattle Weighing over 260 kg
pmc-13431544.creator: Maria Virginia Ralletti, Andrea Beltrame, Elisa Marcucci, Paola D’Angelo, Riccardo Rinnovati, Alessandro Spadari
pmc-13431544.description: Simple SummaryTibial fractures in heavy beef cattle are often considered difficult to treat because of the animals’ size, high costs for the farmer and poor prognosis. This study describes the use of a full limb cast combined with double transfixation pinning to repair tibial fractures in 11 beef cattle weighing between 260 and 480 kg under field conditions.

pmc-13476390.title: G6PD activity patterns and a stable adjusted male median derived from 16 years of clinical laboratory data
pmc-13476390.creator: Muhammad Shariq Shaikh, Zeeshan Ansar Ahmed
pmc-13476390.description: PurposeGlucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency, the most common enzymopathy worldwide, poses significant clinical and public health challenges, particularly in malaria-endemic regions. Despite the importance of quantitative G6PD activity assessments, clinically meaningful deficiency thresholds remain difficult to define owing to biological variability related to age, sex, and X-linked inheritance.

pmc-13494718.title: Default Hospice Consultation in Comfort Measures Orders and Hospice Engagement
pmc-13494718.creator: L. Scott Sussman, John M. Henderson, Nancy Kim
pmc-13494718.description: This quality improvement study examines the association of having a hospice consultation as default for patients given comfort measures orders with hospice engagement. Introduction Hospice improves end-of-life care quality yet remains underutilized, with persistent racial and ethnic access disparities.1,2,3,4 In hospitals, hospice enrollment requires clinician-initiated consultation, creating workflow barriers and referral practice variability.

pmc-13544415.title: Large Language Models for Heterogeneous Data Mining in Liver Disease: Framework Development and Retrospective Validation Study
pmc-13544415.creator: Haiping Zhang, Xinming Li, Kechi Fang, Yinxue Ma, Lijuan Li, Huiping Yan, Yanmin Liu, Yanhua Yu, Jing Wang
pmc-13544415.description: BackgroundDifferentiating among liver disease entities such as autoimmune liver disease (AILD), drug-induced liver injury (DILI), and chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains clinically challenging due to overlapping clinical manifestations and nonspecific laboratory findings. Conventional machine learning (ML) approaches rely mainly on structured laboratory data, whereas free-text clinical reports and other heterogeneous electronic medical record data are often underused.
